title: Fixed-K product-key state-population scaling
question: Does a fixed K=32 product-key retrieval budget preserve target-state retrieval capability as persistent-state population M increases from 64 to 512?
hypothesis: If product-key addressing provides genuinely sparse state computation, a fixed K=32 budget should retain substantial target recall while exhaustive state-scoring cost grows with M.

arms.name: exhaustive_cosine
arms.intervention: score all M persistent states with the fixed width-16 teacher

arms.name: product_key_fixed_k32
arms.intervention: same training-fitted product-key codebooks and factor beam 6 with fixed K=32

decision_rule.condition: report target recall and end-to-end success against exhaustive references at every M level, together with K/M, states scored/M, and arithmetic reduction
decision_rule.licenses: diagnostic evidence about fixed-budget product-key scaling on this synthetic workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: a universal sublinear-compute law, ANN guarantee, or hardware speedup

decision_rule.condition: target recall remains near the fixed exhaustive reference while K/M and scored-state/M fall materially with increasing M
decision_rule.licenses: bounded support for fixed-budget product-key scaling on this workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: broad C5 or general semantic memory claims

held_constant: same 48 training codes versus 16 held-out target codes
same factor size and factor beam
state embeddings are precomputed for exhaustive and selective reference fairness
